$comment: THE EIGHT FBL-140 OUTCOMES, LOCKED BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN, exactly as the architect's order states them. `order_text` is quoted VERBATIM from docs/orders/FBL-140-ORDER.md — the build script read it out of that committed file rather than retyping it, and scripts/check-fbl140-rows.ts refuses a quotation those bytes do not contain, so the acceptance contract cannot carry the implementer's fingerprints. `tests` is filled in as each outcome is proven, and a row naming no test — or naming one that does not exist — fails the gate.

order.phase: FBL-140 — Deal Jacket, Documents, and E-Sign Evidence
order.issued_under: Standing Architect Order SO-001, Master Blueprint Version 3.1 (docs/orders/Car_Dealership_Management_and_Sales_Cloud_Master_Blueprint_v3.1.docx, sha256 c57894f4c0018e7d36afc3e7255eeb17d80b2b3899d5ba44ebd1956a1ee93979)
order.starting_point: main at 6172ba8e1ba99db074d2f7985ca70dd57d6e057d, FBL-120 CLOSED, migration 065 frozen
order.objective: From one exact, current, manager-approved FBL-120 desking version, produce an immutable, version-bound, auditable deal-jacket and document-signing package ready for the later limited F&I and funding workflow. FBL-140 may create the deal-jacket/document aggregate. It must not declare a sale, funding, delivery, sold vehicle, accounting entry, or revenue event.

rows.title: Canonical intake and identity
rows.order_text: 1. Canonical intake and identity Consume the exact approved desking version through FBL-120’s public interface or published fact. Bind tenant, legal entity, rooftop, opportunity, party, selected stock, trade/appraisal context, approved scenario version, and rule versions. Retry and concurrency must converge without duplicate active jackets.

tests.name: opening a jacket binds every canonical reference at the version it carried
a repeated intake converges on the jacket that already exists
two genuinely concurrent intakes converge on one jacket
a deal nothing is approved on cannot have a jacket, and a foreign or missing file is simply not found
the discovery list holds approved deals nobody has opened a jacket for, and drops them once opened
the backstop keys refuse a duplicate active jacket with every service stepped round
when the desk approves a newer version the jacket is stale, assembly refuses, and void-then-open binds the new one

rows.title: Versioned checklist and document requirements
rows.order_text: 2. Versioned checklist and document requirements Resolve requirements from typed, effective-dated legal-entity, rooftop, jurisdiction, transaction-type, and template configuration. Every requirement must show its source and version. Missing required items block progression. Any permitted waiver requires authorized actor, reason, policy version, and, and and evidence.

tests.name: every requirement and template names its source, scope, interval and version, and a sample says it is one
an approval names who and when and what it rests on, or it is not an approval — service and database agree
two versions of one requirement or template cannot both be in force over one instant
missing required items block progression, evidence satisfies, and an optional item never blocks
a waiver is four things from an eligible manager, or it is nothing — service and database agree
a template with no version in force is a render failure the board can see, not a blank document
a rooftop's own requirement beats the tenant-wide one, and an exact transaction type beats 'any'

rows.title: Deterministic package assembly
rows.order_text: 3. Deterministic package assembly Assemble fields from canonical records without operator rekeying or copied shadow truth. Every financial figure must exactly match the approved FBL-120 version and preserve currency and fixed-decimal semantics. Record field provenance and source versions.

tests.name: every financial field is the approved version’s own integer cents, with its currency and its provenance
a stale desk approval is refused at assembly and shows on the board, while the approved figures never move under a jacket

rows.title: Immutable rendering and artifacts
rows.order_text: 4. Immutable rendering and artifacts Render versioned document packages deterministically. Bind each artifact to package version, template version, content hash, MIME type, size, classification, malware result, retention policy, and legal-hold state. A changed input creates a new superseding version; it never mutates a rendered or signed package.

tests.name: rendering is a pure function: same template and fields, same bytes, same digest
the same inputs assembled again write nothing, and every artifact is bound to what the order names
a written package, a rendered document and a blob cannot be edited — the database refuses each
a changed input writes the next version and supersedes the last; the earlier package, its figures and its bytes are intact
an approved template renders its approval and a package of approved templates asks for no review

rows.title: E-sign ceremony and evidence
rows.order_text: 5. E-sign ceremony and evidence Capture electronic-record consent, signer identity and role, signing authority, authentication assurance, intent, exact package version/hash, timestamps, provider delivery records, signature results, and completion certificate. Provider callbacks must be signed, idempotent, replay-safe, and reconcilable. A signer cannot sign a superseded or modified package.

tests.name: sending is a manager’s act that binds the package hash, seats the signers in their lanes, and shows staff no link
the customer views, consents, and signs exactly the hash they were shown — in that order and no other
the dealer signs last, through the staff session the ceremony names, and completion is a document anyone can re-hash
a superseded or modified package takes no signature — the service and the database both refuse
declining ends the ceremony, voids the package and touches nothing that was signed
a provider callback is signed, recorded once, replayed harmlessly, and reconciled against our own evidence
a signing link is a digest in the database and a clock in the hand — expired, foreign and invented tokens all fail closed

rows.title: Lifecycle and operational exceptions
rows.order_text: 6. Lifecycle and operational exceptions Support coherent states equivalent to draft, review-ready, sent, partially signed, signed-complete, voided, expired, and superseded. Terminal states are absorbing except through explicit versioned supersession. Expose actionable queues for missing documents, render failure, rejected or expired signatures, provider failure, and stale approved-desking inputs.

tests.name: draft → review-ready → sent → partially signed → signed-complete, each move attributed and versioned
a manager voids a sent package and its ceremony; the signer’s link stops answering; nothing is deleted
terminal states are absorbing: the database refuses to revive a voided package or void a signed one
the clock expires a ceremony nobody finished — through the worker’s own pass, once — and the board queues it
the board carries every queue the order names, and says what it does not know

rows.title: Authorization, isolation, and privacy
rows.order_text: 7. Authorization, isolation, and privacy Enforce tenant and rooftop RLS, tenant-qualified parent binding, non-disclosing authorization, optimistic concurrency, idempotency, audit/outbox atomicity, short-lived artifact access, PII-safe logs/events, retention, export, and legal holds. Sales staff, managers, customer signers, support actors, and system/provider callbacks must use distinct authority lanes.

tests.name: a salesperson opens, assembles and readies; only a manager waives, reviews, sends and voids — and the refusal explains nothing
the support lane is the administrator’s alone: retention, legal hold and export refuse a manager
a package is reached through its own id, and somebody else’s package, jacket or ceremony is not found
a repeated command with one key is applied once and answered twice; a stale expected_version is a conflict
a document leaves only through a short-lived grant, which is counted and then shut
the customer’s lane is a token, not a session: it signs the exact package, and a staff token opens nothing on it
the provider’s lane is a signature over the raw body: unsigned is refused before it is read, a replay converges
the event ledger, the outbox and the audit trail carry ids and digests — never a name, an address or a link
this phase still cannot create a sale, a funded deal or a delivery, because there is nowhere to put one
an unauthenticated caller reaches nothing on the staff surface
every table this phase adds is secured, and a session without a dealership sees none of it
one dealership cannot read, edit or delete another’s jacket, package, documents or signatures
a write that names another dealership is refused by the policy, not merely filtered
the blob store is reachable only through a dealership’s own document rows
the privileged resolver is not executable by the runtime, and the ordinary one is dealership-bound

rows.title: Real persisted user journey

tests.name: all eight outcomes are proven, and each names tests this repository declares
the outcomes are quoted verbatim from the committed order, not paraphrased from memory
the journey was walked in the shipped console and signing page by four different people
every bullet of Outcome 8 has a stage that shows it
every cross-lane attempt was refused in the words a missing record gets
nothing in the journey was reached by typing an identifier
the staff view carries hashes and figures, and says NOT_YET_AVAILABLE for what this phase lacks
every FBL-140 control the registries declare names a test that exists, and every anchor occurs exactly once
the delivery report names the order, the seam, the five lanes and every outcome

exclusions: FBL-140 exclusions. FBL-140 must not implement: credit applications, bureau pulls, lender routing or decisions; F&I product menus or contracting; funding or receivable approval; title or registration completion; vehicle delivery or sold-inventory transition; payment settlement or accounting posting; gross, commission, or revenue recognition; advanced digital retail; Fixed Operations expansion. Do not invent legal forms or claim that sample templates are jurisdictionally approved. Store the exact template source, approval status, jurisdiction, effective interval, and accountable approver.
binary_proof: FBL-140 binary proof. One complete local battery; all declared runtime and database-control mutation registries with zero survivors and green baselines; fresh and upgraded database convergence; proof that migrations 000–065 remain byte-identical and only forward migration 066+ is added; persisted multi-identity UI journey; artifact hash/version and signature replay proof; exact-SHA CI; Ready status and merge of the exact verified SHA; green post-merge main state.
